sources.name: LAPD Crime Data from 2020 to Present (Socrata id 2nrs-mtv8) - now renamed 'Crime Data from 2020 to 2024'
sources.contains: Incident-level LAPD crime records with lat/lon. Socrata metadata (https://data.lacity.org/api/views/2nrs-mtv8.json) confirms columns: dr_no, date_rptd, date_occ, time_occ, area, area_name, rpt_dist_no, part_1_2, crm_cd, crm_cd_desc, mocodes, vict_age, vict_sex, vict_descent, premis_cd, premis_desc, weapon_used_cd, weapon_desc, status, status_desc, crm_cd_1..4, location (text, hundred block), cross_street, lat (number), lon (number). Because lat/lon are plain numeric columns (no Socrata 'point' column), a radius query must be done with a SoQL bounding box on lat/lon (e.g. $where=lat between .. and lon between ..) via https://data.lacity.org/resource/2nrs-mtv8.json, then filtered to a circle client-side; rpt_dist_no allows aggregation by LAPD reporting district. Area 01 = Central Division covers DTLA/Skid Row.
sources.granularity: incident, hundred-block geocoded, LAPD reporting district
headline_datapoints: rowsUpdatedAt 2026-03-04T17:17:20Z; notice: 'the Crime Data from 2020 to Present dataset will no longer be updated. It will remain available on the portal for historical reference only.'

must_ask_hmp: The actual offer / LOI from Lee & Associates (David Brandt): base rent, whether NNN or full service, CAM/tax/insurance pass-throughs, term, escalations, security deposit, free rent, TI allowance, renewal options, and whether the ~$10,000/mo figure in the proposal is base rent or all-in.
Whether the space is still available (LoopNet shows 'no longer being advertised') and whether the landlord is marketing 768 alone or 768 & 772 (16,887 SF) together.

Landlord identity (likely '768 Ceres LLC') and stance on lithium-ion battery charging/storage, e-moped repair, indoor fleet parking, generator/EV charger installation, LAFD hazardous-materials and Title 24 / electrical permitting, and any use restrictions in the lease.
Confirmation of electrical service (listing says 400A / 240V / 3-phase / 4-wire) vs HMP's planned charging load, and whether the landlord will allow panel upgrades.
Existing security infrastructure at the site (listing mentions an 'electrical yard gate'), fenced yard dimensions, camera/alarm wiring, and any incident history the landlord or neighbors can share.
HMP's insurance broker quotes for this address (property, liability, battery/fire) and any carrier exclusions for the 90021 Skid Row-adjacent area.
HMP's own rider data: where target couriers live and start shifts, current SF depot usage patterns (visits/day, dwell time) to judge rider convenience vs Koreatown/Westlake alternatives.
surprises: Asking rent is inconsistent across mirrors: LoopNet snippet '$19.20 per square foot per year'; PropertyShark '$1.20/SF/MO ... Full Service'; combined 768 & 772 listing '$1.40/SF/MO ($16.80/SF/YR) ... Full Service'. Arithmetic only: $1.20 x 8,443 SF = about $10,132/mo (matches the CONTEXT's ~$10,000/mo), whereas $19.20/SF/yr x 8,443 SF = about $13,509/mo. Two mirrors label the lease 'Full Service' rather than NNN.
At least one LoopNet listing for the address states the property 'is no longer being advertised on LoopNet.com' - the space may be leased or the listing pulled.
768 Ceres appears to be one of two twin 2015 buildings (768 & 772, 16,887 SF, 0.42 ac) marketed together on at least one aggregator - possible expansion option or landlord preference to lease both.

The LAPD 'Crime Data from 2020 to Present' dataset named in the CONTEXT is frozen: renamed 'Crime Data from 2020 to 2024', last rows updated 2026-03-04, 'will no longer be updated'; 2024-2026 crime must come from the LAPD NIBRS Offenses dataset (bi-weekly since Oct 2024).

Listing marketing describes the site as 'Arts District & Downtown Adjacent' in the 'AIR - CBD' submarket, not Skid Row or Fashion District; meanwhile 2026 reporting shows Downtown/Skid Row homelessness up 23% (3,427 to 4,215) and Central Division aggravated assaults up 25%, and RAND says the official Skid Row count is undercounted by ~39%.

Kidder Mathews Q2 2026 puts Central LA industrial at $1.34 PSF/mo NNN and the 'Los Angeles' city submarket at $1.52 PSF/mo NNN, with LA-wide rents down 32.4% over 36 months per CBRE - i.e. a falling-rent market at the time of negotiation.
